mechanism: Bumetanide causes electrolyte depletion (hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia) which increases risk of cardiac arrhythmias and orthostatic hypotension; prochlorperazine potentiates these effects through anticholinergic activity, alpha-blockade, and direct myocardial depression.
action: Monitor serum electrolytes regularly, assess orthostatic vital signs, consider EKG if prolonged QT risk, and ensure adequate potassium/magnesium supplementation; use lowest effective doses of both agents.
